skill.name: camera-prompt-quickcheck
skill.description: Instant pre-flight diagnostic linter for AI video prompts (Runway, Kling, Sora, Veo, Seedance). Detects missing camera mechanisms, dolly-vs-zoom confusion, dual-motion conflicts, vague fluff, and missing end-settle states before wasting generation credits.
skill.summary: Check camera movement, pacing, and framing in AI video prompts before generation.
skill.author: 287523023qq-hue

security_audit.summary: All 38 static matches were false positives: Markdown notation, inert Python strings, test fixtures, or local linter calls with shell execution disabled. No evidence of command injection or data exfiltration was found in the reviewed paths. Optional prompt echo can expose downstream assistants to untrusted instructions, even when Markdown formatting is escaped.

remediation.issue: Optional prompt echo can pass untrusted instructions to downstream assistants.
remediation.suggestion: Remove full prompt echo from agent-facing reports. If a preview is needed, show it only in a separate human review interface.

semantic_findings.title: Optional Prompt Echo Exposes Downstream Assistants to Untrusted Instructions
semantic_findings.description: When prompt echo is enabled, JSON preserves the normalized prompt and Markdown escapes formatting only. A downstream assistant could still follow instructions embedded in the echoed text.

content.user_title: Check Camera Directions in AI Video Prompts
content.value_statement: Ambiguous camera directions can lead to video generations that miss the intended shot. Check movement, pacing, framing, and the final shot before you generate.
actual_capabilities: Recognizes common camera directions such as dolly, pan, tilt, orbit, and static shot.
Flags ambiguous zoom wording, unlabeled dolly and zoom combinations, and three or more detected motion axes.
Checks for pacing, starting composition or framing anchors, and an explicit end state.
Returns a score out of 100, diagnostic rule codes, and suggested fixes.
Produces Markdown or JSON reports locally and omits the full prompt by default.
limitations: The rules match wording and may miss unfamiliar terms, negation, or movements intended for separate shots.
The score reflects phrasing checks and does not predict how a particular video model will render the shot.
The skill does not generate video, inspect footage, or plan transitions between keyframes.
The bundled linter suggests changes but does not rewrite the prompt itself.

use_cases.title: Check a First Video Prompt
use_cases.description: Find missing movement, pacing, or ending cues before submitting a prompt to a video generator.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Product Reveal
use_cases.description: Distinguish camera travel from an optical zoom while preserving product framing and the final reveal.

use_cases.title: Review Prompts Before Handoff
use_cases.description: Check each shot separately and share rule codes and suggested changes with a production team.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Shot
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this camera prompt: [shot prompt]. Give me the score and the most important change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Camera Move
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [shot prompt] describes camera travel or optical zoom. My intent is [intended movement]. Suggest the smallest change that makes it clear.
prompt_templates.scenario: A prompt uses zoom to describe a change in framing.

prompt_templates.title: Revise and Recheck a Shot
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [shot prompt] for competing movements, missing pacing, and weak framing cues. Suggest a minimal revision that preserves [creative intent], then check it again.
prompt_templates.scenario: A complex shot needs revision without changing its purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Shot Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [variant A] and [variant B] separately. Compare their scores, rule codes, and suggested fixes. Recommend the variant that best preserves [shot goal].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison before choosing a production prompt.

output_examples.input: Cinematic zoom in toward the lighthouse.
output: Score: 10 out of 100. High risk for unclear camera directions.
The prompt lacks a clear camera mechanism, pace, framing anchor, and end state.
Specify a dolly in for camera travel or an optical zoom for a focal length change.

output_examples.input: Starting from a wide shot, slowly dolly in toward the lighthouse. Keep the horizon level and settle into a close-up.
output: Detected movement: dolly in. No diagnostic findings.

best_practices: Check one shot at a time so separate moves are not mistaken for competing camera directions.
Specify the main movement, pace, starting composition, and final framing.
Use the findings to revise the prompt, then run the check again.
anti_patterns: Using zoom in when the intended result is physical camera travel.
Stacking several movements into one shot without a clear primary move.
Treating a high score as a guarantee of video quality.

faq.question: Does the linter generate video?
faq.answer: No. It checks prompt text before you submit it to a video generator.

faq.question: Does the linter need an API key or network access?
faq.answer: No. The bundled linter runs locally with Python 3 and uses only the standard library.

faq.question: Can I use it with different video generators?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks general camera wording for prompts intended for tools such as Runway, Kling, Sora, Veo, or Seedance.

faq.question: What score counts as a pass?
faq.answer: A score of 85 or higher is a pass. This reflects the prompt rules, not a guarantee of how the video will look.

faq.question: Does the report repeat my full prompt?
faq.answer: The full prompt is omitted by default. Keep optional prompt echo disabled when sending diagnostics to an assistant.

faq.question: Does it support prompts other than English?
faq.answer: The rules recognize selected Chinese camera and framing terms as well as English. Coverage is limited to recognized wording.
